title: Free-hand sketching
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Sketching lines and 2D shapes (outcomes c and d) is marked on the learner's sketch with the rubric; the questions test the principles and techniques.

skills.key_step: The learner explains the principles of free-hand sketching: drawn by hand without instruments, start with light lines, block in the overall shape and proportions first, then firm the correct lines and add detail; keep the pencil soft and sharp.

floor.question: Name a four-sided figure with all sides equal.

representations: a sketch in three stages: light, proportion, firm
a bottle with its overall box shape
steps: Firm the right lines and add detail.

board.do: Sketch a bottle in light lines with its overall box shape.
Point at the light box around it.
board.say: Why start with this before the label?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say proportion and whole shape first.
Firm the outline and add the label.

listen_for: Drawing with a ruler and compass
misconceptions.repair: Show a quick freehand sketch of a stool made in one minute; explain it is for ideas, before exact drawing.
Sketch light lines that can be changed, then darken the right ones; show a pressed wrong line that cannot be removed.

listen_for: Rub out every line at once
misconceptions.ask: What helps a sketch stay tidy?
misconceptions.repair: Leave light construction lines; darken only the correct ones; rub out at the end if needed.

misconceptions.ask: What do you look at first when sketching a bottle?
misconceptions.repair: Block in the whole shape and its proportions with light lines first, then add the details.

checks.question: How do you start a sketch?
What do you look at first when sketching an object?

skills.key_step: The learner names and uses sketching techniques: lines between marked points with light steady strokes, the box (crating) method, the centreline method for symmetrical objects, the hand-compass and square methods for circles, and shading by hatching, cross-hatching and stippling; the sketched lines and 2D shapes are marked with the rubric.

floor.question: Should the first lines of a sketch be light or dark?

representations: three shaded squares: hatching, cross-hatching, stippling
a circle in a light square
steps: Sketch straight lines between two points.
Use the box method for a shape.
Use the centreline method for a symmetrical object.
contexts: shading a box to show its form

board.do: Draw three squares side by side.

board.say: Shade it by cross-hatching. What will you draw?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say two sets of crossing lines.
Shade the other two by hatching and stippling.

misconceptions.repair: Shade three squares: hatching (parallel lines), cross-hatching (crossing lines), stippling (dots); label each.

listen_for: One set of lines across the shape
misconceptions.repair: Draw one set of parallel lines, then a second set crossing them: that is cross-hatching.

misconceptions.ask: Which method draws a circle with the hand turning about a fixed finger?
misconceptions.repair: Sketch a circle twice: in a light square (box method) and by turning the paper about a fixed finger (hand compass).

misconceptions.ask: Which object suits the centreline method?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a centreline, mark equal distances on both sides; try it on a bottle and on a stone.

misconceptions.ask: How is a long straight line sketched freehand?
misconceptions.repair: Mark two points, keep the eye on the end point and draw with the whole arm in light strokes; compare with a scratchy line.

checks.question: Which method suits a symmetrical bottle?
